scope: Correct status interpretation and messages; preserve driver admission, capture behavior, UI layout and styles. Native mode parser shared by scan selection and execution.
changes: Selection retains per-phy monitor refusal instead of suggesting refresh. Unknown mode evidence remains unconfirmed and is not admitted.
Dependency command states and install queues remain command-level evidence. Details separately explain unsupported, mixed and unknown radio capabilities; remove old and modern hcx readiness promises.
Background status checks the lock PID plus an exact known script path argument. A random hcxdumptool process no longer makes our script appear running.
Both start entry points emit a structured script-start event. The console no longer depends on Chinese success text. Badge, banner, summary, metric and tooltip report script status only.

reviews.focus: Shared capability parsing, three-radio unsupported/mixed/unknown evidence, dependency notes and both startup paths
Cross-entry regression for radio usage, takeover, scan, DFS, dependency partial installation, built-in package, cleanup and startup
Actual customer ZIP replay, Debian shell identity probe, Windows light/dark page rendering, event/lifecycle review and final affected tests
reviews.issues_found_and_fixed: Message-driven console trigger and remaining summary/metric claims were removed. Old text assertions updated to new semantics.

platform_validation.windows: Qt offscreen rendered with explicitly registered Microsoft YaHei; badge and banner fit. Test process font database was initially empty; no product font change made.
platform_validation.debian12: Actual /proc script probe passed matching PID, invalid/dead/missing locks and foreign hcxdumptool identity. Temporary processes terminated. Desktop startup/render/exit remain unverified because PySide6 is unavailable.
platform_validation.router: Read-only customer logs only; no live router mutation or test performed.

performance: No added refresh query or polling interval. Existing status query replaces broad process listing with a bounded cmdline read. No new dependency installation.
compatibility: Native iw capability interpretation and proc identity are driver/version independent. Kernel v5.10 docs read for the reported kernel. This is not a claim that all OpenWrt/hardware combinations have been tested. No radio number guessing or driver replacement.

followup_recheck.request: Repeat three review rounds and verify with official sources.

findings: Legacy autocap.sh uses .autocap.lock; the prior single-lock probe missed it.
Page dispose did not unsubscribe all service events.
round_1.fixes: Pair both supported script names with their own locks; scope and release all service connections.

round_2.focus: Cross-entry failure, cancellation, unknown ownership and lifecycle regression.

round_3.official_docs: Qt documents that already queued events can still arrive after disconnect. Exact runtime Qt 6.3.2 implementation also posts and dispatches MetaCall events.
round_3.reproduced: With the log panel visible, a worker log queued before dispose changed the disposed page. Regression failed before active-slot guard.
round_3.fix: Common active_service_slot combines typed Qt slots with disposed-page guard; store connection handles and disconnect only owned subscriptions. Preserve QObject receiver and main-thread delivery.
round_3.thread_affinity: Worker emission queued; live page callback runs on UI thread; disposed page ignores queued notification.
round_3.resource_check: 12 real Qt page create/dispose/delete cycles; all weak references cleared after normal deferred deletion.
round_3.debian12: Real proc identity probe for current and legacy scripts passed matching, wrong, missing, invalid and dead locks; child processes cleaned up.

followup_recheck.boundaries: Source only. No layout/style change, timer workaround or router writes. Live router and Debian desktop startup/render/exit remain pending. Qt guidance pages are current docs; exact Qt 6.3.2 source and runtime regression independently verify applicability.

additional_reference_review.request: Another three review rounds grounded in official references.

rounds.conclusion: Supported interface types derive from wiphy.interface_modes. brcmfmac advertises monitor only under its MONITOR_FLAG capability. Therefore actual device evidence controls admission; neither model nor installed commands imply support. The upstream baseline does not prove the exact vendor snapshot has identical code.

Enabled startup links, a matching live script PID and successful capture are distinct facts. Current/legacy lock names and exact script arguments remain paired. No kill or configuration mutation was added by the probe.

rounds.topic: Qt notifications, thread affinity and disposal
rounds.conclusion: All 14 service receivers have active typed slots. Owned connection handles are disconnected; queued callbacks are rejected after disposal. Actual Qt 6.3.2 regression confirms main-thread delivery and disposed-page rejection.

validation.debian12_actual_identity_probe: passed for current and legacy names; wrong/missing/invalid/dead locks rejected
